title: Verzasca (Lago di Vogorno)
place: Lower Valle Verzasca between the Contra dam and Corippo
summary: A high arch dam at the mouth of the Valle Verzasca drowned the valley floor below Vogorno, with the hamlet of Pioda, the road and farmland.
why: In the lower Valle Verzasca the river flowed through a narrow valley. Below Vogorno lay the road, fields and the hamlet of Pioda, where about thirty people lived.

Verzasca SA was founded in 1960 to use more water of the Verzasca. From 1961 to 1965 it built one of the highest dams in Switzerland at the mouth of the valley. Today the company belongs one third to the canton of Ticino and two thirds to the city of Lugano.

The lake reaches into the communes of Vogorno, Mergoscia and Corippo. When the water level is low in dry periods, the bare shores change the landscape. This affects the people and the tourism of the valley.
gained: Verzasca SA runs two power stations in the valley: the large plant at the foot of the dam and the small Tenero plant (since 1908).
The company is fully public. The shareholders gave the tax share of the company seat to the communes; most of it goes to Gordola, Tenero and Minusio.
lost: The lake covered several houses and much farmland in Vogorno, and the hamlet of Pioda with about thirty people. 64 of the 105 families of Vogorno were affected.
The old road along the valley floor disappeared under the water.
In dry periods the low lake level harms the landscape, the inhabitants and tourism, even when the minimum levels of the concession are kept.

title: Saane (Schiffenensee / Lac de Schiffenen)
place: Saane valley between Fribourg and Schiffenen, west of Düdingen (Guin)
summary: An arch dam at Schiffenen turned 13.5 km of the Saane below Fribourg into a reservoir; land and the old spa hamlet of Bad Bonn went under water.
why: Below Fribourg the Saane wound through a deep valley. The hamlet of Bad Bonn lay at the river; from the 17th to the 19th century it was a popular spa.
The Fribourg power company (Entreprises électriques fribourgeoises, today Groupe E) built an arch dam 47 m high at Schiffenen. The dam was finished in 1963 and the power plant started in 1964.
A road on top of the dam links the Sense and Lake districts. The HLS describes the lake in the early 21st century as an area for leisure.
gained: The power plant makes on average 133 GWh (133 million kWh) of electricity per year.
The road on the dam crest links the districts of Sense and Lake.
The HLS describes the lake in the early 21st century as an area for leisure, with a golf course and a marina.
lost: The lake covered 1,400 poses of land (an old local unit of area) and the hamlet of Bad Bonn.
About 13.5 km of the free-flowing Saane below Fribourg became a lake.

title: Spöl (Lago di Livigno and the Swiss National Park)
place: Punt dal Gall on the Swiss-Italian border; Spöl valley in the Swiss National Park down to Zernez
summary: The Punt dal Gall dam made the Lago di Livigno on the border; below it the Spöl flows through the Swiss National Park with only the water the power plants release.
why: The Spöl rises in the Livigno valley in Italy and flows through the Swiss National Park to the Inn at Zernez. The Engadiner Kraftwerke (Engadine power plants) wanted to use its water and that of the Inn.

From 1965 to 1969 they built the 130 m high Punt dal Gall arch dam. Half of the dam stands in Switzerland and half in Italy, but most of the lake lies in Italy. The lake is the main store of the power plants. Its water goes to a pumped storage plant at Ova Spin and then to power stations at Pradella and Martina.

Just below the dam the Spöl enters the National Park. A small power station at the dam releases residual water (water left in the river). Since 2000 the plants also make one to three artificial floods each year, up to 40 m³/s, to keep the stream more natural.
gained: The lake holds 164 million m³ of usable water. The three power stages have about 400 MW of turbine power.
The artificial floods move gravel again and improve the river bed and its life in the residual water stretches.
lost: The maps of 1964 and today show that the lake covered the valley floor of the Spöl and the lower Val del Gallo on the Italian side.
The reservoir holds back all the gravel from the upper valley and dampens the floods. Some water is also taken out of the Spöl catchment to the Adda in Italy.
At Easter 2013 the residual water supply failed because of technical problems. Mud entered the stream, and thousands of fish died over about 6 km in the National Park.

title: Tamina (Gigerwaldsee reservoir)
place: Calfeisental between St. Martin and Vättis
summary: A 147 m high arch dam in the Calfeisental made the Gigerwaldsee; it filled the narrow valley floor of the Tamina below the old Walser hamlet of St. Martin.
why: The Calfeisental is a high side valley above Vättis. Walser settlers lived there from at least 1346, but they gave up living there all year in the 16th or 17th century. Since then the valley has been used only for alpine farming and, later, tourism. The old chapel of St. Martin still stands.

The Kraftwerke Sarganserland company was founded in 1961. From 1971 to 1978 it built a storage power system in the Calfeisental and the Weisstannental. The Gigerwald arch dam was built from 1973 to 1975. HLS dates the lake to 1976; the plant started in 1977.
The lake is a seasonal store. It also takes water from the Weisstannental. The water drives power stations at Mapragg and Sarelli. Water can be pumped back up from the Mapragg basin into the lake.
gained: The lake holds about 33-36 million m³ of water. The Mapragg power station has three turbines of 93.3 MW and three pumps of 53 MW.
lost: The lake covered about 70 ha of the narrow valley floor of the Tamina, with alpine pastures, between St. Martin and the gorge at Gigerwald.
Water from the Weisstannental is led away into the lake.
